analysis:
This batch has two documentation-only changes: the new changelog fragment changelog.d/qwen-gdn-prompt-kernel.md (lines 1-4) and a new paragraph in docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 595-611). Both describe a Gated DeltaNet prompt-prefill kernel for qwen3_5, qwen3_5_moe and prism_hadamard_qwen35 models. The kernel itself (libs/mlx-swift-lm/.../GatedDelta.swift) was not supplied, so this pass cannot confirm the described behavior.

The docs claim:
- The new kernel is used only for unmasked prompt windows of 16 or more tokens.
- The first window per dtype and head geometry runs a GPU probe. The new kernel is kept only if it matches gated_delta_step bit for bit; otherwise the stock kernel runs.
- Decode, MTP verification and masked updates always use the stock kernel.
- DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED switches back to the stock kernel or forces a candidate.

Security relevance:
- T-041 and TB-007: bit-exact recurrent state matters because prefix-cache checkpoints depend on it. If the probe were wrong or incomplete, cached checkpoints could be inconsistent. This would be a correctness or integrity risk, not a new confidentiality channel, and it can only be checked in the code.
- The probe uses a fixed window, so no tenant data is involved. That reduces cross-tenant leakage concern.
- The faster prefill slightly changes TTFT timing. That is the same kind as the already-accepted SEC-035 oracle.
- The env var is operator-controlled and the changelog says the LaunchAgent does not receive it. This adds no remote or consumer-reachable surface.

No regressions or threat-model gaps are evident from the documentation alone. The next pass should check the GatedDelta.swift probe logic: whether a fixed probe covers all state shapes and whether a wrong kernel selection fails closed.
